rationale: Re-review reason: depends_on declared (DI-28 -> DI-20); DI-28 text and test unchanged. Upstream context: DI-20 (record a verdict hash-pinned to the current verifying-test source) is the pin whose scope DI-28 parameterizes -- the test drives the real record_verdict over a real tagged test file, so scope is exercised through the recorder, not only the reconciler. All 4 recorded probes re-executed one at a time via rdm story mutation-probe, all still KILLED, plus 2 new recorder-side probes (KILLED). Clauses: (1) each verdict records its hash scope -- record field `"hash_scope": hash_scope` -> `"module"` KILLED (new: a function-selected verdict recorded as module goes stale on the helper edit); (2) module scope by default -- `DEFAULT_SCOPE = SCOPE_MODULE` -> `SCOPE_FUNCTION` KILLED; (3) module scope = the full source files containing the verifying tests -- module hashing `texts.append(Path(path).read_text(...))` -> `texts.append("")` KILLED (an untagged-helper edit must stale the default pin); (4) function scope selectable -- recorder pinning at module regardless of the selected scope (`scope=hash_scope` -> `scope=faithfulness.SCOPE_MODULE` in record_verdict) KILLED (new; the function pin must survive the helper edit); (5) staleness judged per verdict at its recorded scope -- reconcile `expected[scope] = current_hashes(..., scope)` -> `SCOPE_MODULE` KILLED; (6) legacy verdicts (no hash_scope) honored as function-scoped -- fold fallback `else SCOPE_FUNCTION` -> `else SCOPE_MODULE` KILLED (hand-written legacy record must stay FAITHFUL). Known limitation carried from prior reviews (not a DI clause gap): the second _edit_helper() call is a no-op because the first already rewrote its search string, so 'function pin survives a helper edit' compares against an already-edited file; the function-scope clauses are nonetheless pinned by the kills in (1) and (4). All clauses covered.
